   - Detailed description of the chosen/best idea, including rationale, pseudocode, and implementation notes

The report must be focused, technically accurate. Being concise with 200-500 words without trivial and redundant information.
Support all claims with evidence and references, and remain tightly aligned with the target problem.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis accesses the item embedding table through `item_emb.weight` and sequence representations through `log2feats(sequence)`. Model internals are not supplied, so the encoder architecture and representation computation cannot be established. The probe uses features for every sequence position; it does not explicitly extract a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the supplied model or compatibility view, plus its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Only metadata is subsequently queried; reviews and stored histories are unused.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` invokes two probes. Training batches supply `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with shape `B × L`. Sequences are converted to NumPy before `log2feats`; positive and negative IDs are stacked into `B × L × 2` candidates for `predict_score(features, items)`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal pairwise cosine similarities, and maps the mean to `[0,1]`. Higher values suggest directional collapse; approximately 0.5 corresponds to near-zero average cosine.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower tenth-percentile positive-minus-negative score across up to ten batches. Higher values indicate stronger separation, including difficult positions.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction of margins below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top 20 categories.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, or sensitivity tests occur. Negative candidates come directly from the loader. Margin evaluation disables gradients and sets evaluation mode without restoring the previous mode.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The returned dictionary contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting a downstream JSON interpretation with status, findings, implications, and evidence.

These probes assess embedding geometry and sampled training-pair separation, not validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, or causal sequence sensitivity. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Empty observations yield zeros that can appear healthy. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists remain empty; no category information should be invented.

A practical diagnostic design suggested by these findings: freeze the trained model and candidate set; remove recent interactions, repeated occurrences, or explicitly defined isolated events; compare each intervention with equal-size random removals, additionally matching position or popularity where feasible. Reserve chronological suffixes, train from fresh initialization on earlier prefixes, and evaluate each target using only its preceding history. Exclude reserved suffixes from training inputs, positive targets, and interaction-derived statistics. Use a common timestamp cutoff when claiming globally future prediction. For cross-fitting, each scored target needs a model fitted without that target or later information; ordinary random folds do not enforce chronology. Fine-tuning the contaminated checkpoint does not establish exclusion. These auxiliary experiments leave the official benchmark splits and evaluator unchanged. [Cross-fitting construction](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658738/).

Predictive validity requires another separation: define diagnostic metrics and their predicted intervention gains on development variants, then freeze that rule before evaluating previously unseen model variants. Compare predictions against measured changes in the prescribed macro validation HR@10, using paired candidates/users; report rank correlation, gain-sign accuracy, and uncertainty. Input-perturbation sensitivity alone does not establish that an architecture or training change will help. Treat this as a proposed validation design, not an established SASRec result; repeated adaptation to the same validation scores introduces selection bias. [Model-selection overfitting](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).

---

SASRec adds learned absolute slot embeddings; its reference evaluator keeps the latest L events, left-pads, and reads the final slot. Consequently, deleting nonterminal event j and right-aligning shifts surviving events before j one slot right; later events remain fixed. Recent deletion therefore shifts more events than earlier deletion: equal deletion counts do not control positional disturbance. Freeze the already-truncated window before perturbing; deleting from full history first can introduce an older event. These implications follow from the [model](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py) and [input construction](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/util.py).

Recommended diagnostic controls: preserve the terminal occurrence, delete occurrence indices rather than item IDs, and compare equal-size deletions within each user. Repeated IDs may retain removed information elsewhere; stratify by repetition. Specify whether random controls include recent-treatment indices: unrestricted sampling estimates an ordinary random-deletion baseline, whereas disjoint sampling estimates deletion outside the recent region. Overlap makes some comparisons identical; report overlap and short-history exclusions. Match deletion count, history length, repetition and item frequency where feasible; exact matching on shifted positions usually precludes a distinct deletion control, so recency and positional effects remain entangled. Fix seeds, sampled indices, users and candidates; report paired validation HR@10 changes by category and macro-average.

For stronger separation, compare compact deletion with position-preserving removal: retain surviving position IDs and explicitly block removed keys/values at every layer. In-place padding requires checking actual attention masks; zero item embeddings alone can leave positional signals. Content-only ablation retains positional embeddings but creates artificial inputs. A learned MASK token is another intervention, but SASRec lacks BERT4Rec’s [mask-training objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690). These proposed controls measure model sensitivity, not causal user preference; differences between interventions also include nonlinear attention and distribution-shift effects.

---

Evidence supports perturbation sensitivity as a robustness diagnostic, but I found no direct validation that it predicts out-of-sample HR@10 gains across architectures, losses, and negative samplers—or adds predictive value beyond popularity, last-item, recency-weighted transitions, and training margins. [Rank List Sensitivity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12686) measures recommendation changes after training-data perturbations; this differs from perturbing inference histories. [Cascade-guided adversarial training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.05492) investigates robustness and accuracy, but successful robustness training does not establish sensitivity as a transferable model-selection signal. Sensitivity can reflect useful dependence on history or harmful instability; its direction needs empirical calibration.

Simpler controls deserve priority. [Spotify’s controlled benchmark study](https://www.research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) found history-aware pairwise models outperforming both Transformer reproductions on four of five datasets, using NDCG@10; this supports transition baselines, not an HR@10 sensitivity predictor. Proposed validation: predefine deletion, truncation, and shuffling probes, including shuffling that preserves the last item; measure incremental prediction of HR@10 improvement beyond popularity, last-item, recency-weighted transitions, and training margins. Hold out entire architecture/loss/sampler families when assessing diagnostic transfer. Normalize margins or use rank-based versions because score scales differ.

Repeatedly selecting on the same 800 validation users risks adaptive overfitting. Predeclare search budgets and selection rules, record every trial, compare paired user outcomes with category-stratified uncertainty, and reserve hidden test evaluation for the frozen winner. Fixed seeds improve comparability, not independence; [adaptive-holdout research](https://research.ibm.com/publications/the-reusable-holdout-preserving-validity-in-adaptive-data-analysis) explains the distinction. Preserve the pinned 99-negative evaluator: [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings. Treat full-catalog unseen-item recommendations as a separate diagnostic, not equivalent accuracy evidence; any permitted supplemental validation should report both protocols separately.
